C74-LOM-DEVICE.text: This class represents a MIDI or audio device in Live.
live_set tracks N devices M chains L devices K
live_set tracks N devices M return_chains L devices K
Only automatable parameters are accessible. See DeviceParameter to learn how to modify them.
0 for a single device 1 for a device Rack
Get the original name of the device (e.g. Operator, Auto Filter).
Live device type such as MidiChord, Operator, Limiter, MxDeviceAudioEffect, or PluginDevice.
0 = either the device itself or its enclosing Rack device is off.
This is the string shown in the title bar of the device.
The type of the device. Possible types are: 0 = undefined, 1 = instrument, 2 = audio_effect, 4 = midi_effect.
1 for devices that support the AB Compare feature. 0 otherwise. Available since Live 12.3.
1 if the device has compare preset B loaded. 0 otherwise. (Only relevant if can_compare_ab, otherwise errors.) Available since Live 12.3.
Parameters: script_index [int] bank_index [int] (This is related to hardware control surfaces and is usually not relevant.)
Save the device state to the other compare AB slot. (Only relevant if can_compare_ab, otherwise errors.) Available since Live 12.3.

1 = the device is shown collapsed in the device chain.

C74-LOM-DEVICEPARAMETER.text: This class represents an (automatable) parameter within a MIDI or audio device. To modify a device parameter, set its value property or send its object ID to live.remote~.
live_set tracks N devices M parameters L
Get the automation state of the parameter. 0 = no automation. 1 = automation active. 2 = automation overridden.
Get the default value for this parameter. Only available for parameters that aren't quantized (see is_quantized).

1 = the parameter value can be modified directly by the user, by sending set to a live.object, by automation or by an assigned MIDI message or keystroke. Parameters can be disabled because they are macro-controlled, or they are controlled by a live-remote~ object, or because Live thinks that they should not be moved.
1 for booleans and enums 0 for int/float parameters Although parameters like MidiPitch.Pitch appear quantized to the user, they actually have an is_quantized value of 0.
The short parameter name as shown in the (closed) automation chooser.
The name of a Macro parameter before its assignment.

The active state of the parameter. 0 = the parameter is active and can be changed. 1 = the parameter can be changed but isn't active, so changes won't have an audible effect. 2 = the parameter cannot be changed.
The internal value between min and max. Use display_value for the value as visible in the GUI.
The value as visible in the GUI.
Get a list of the possible values for this parameter. Only available for parameters that are quantized (see is_quantized).
Parameter: value [float] Returns: [symbol] String representation of the specified value.
Returns: [symbol] String representation of the current parameter value.

C74-LOM-MIXERDEVICE.text: This class represents a mixer device in Live. It provides access to volume, panning and other DeviceParameter objects. See DeviceParameter to learn how to modify them.
The Track's Left Split Stereo Pan Parameter.
The Track's Right Split Stereo Pan Parameter.
0 = A, 1 = none, 2 = B [not in master track]
Access to the Track mixer's pan mode: 0 = Stereo, 1 = Split Stereo.

C74-LOM-RACKDEVICE.text: This class represents a Live Rack Device. A RackDevice is a type of Device, meaning that it has all the children, properties and functions that a Device has. Listed below are members unique to RackDevice.
Convenience accessor for the Rack's chain selector.
All 128 Drum Pads for the topmost Drum Rack. Inner Drum Racks return a list of 0 entries.
All 16 visible DrumPads for the topmost Drum Rack. Inner Drum Racks return a list of 0 entries.
1 = The Rack contains an instrument device that is capable of showing its chains in Session View.
1 = the device is a Drum Rack with pads. A nested Drum Rack is a Drum Rack without pads. Only available for Drum Racks.
1 = any of a Rack's Macros are mapped to a parameter.
1 = The Rack contains an instrument device that is showing its chains in Session View.
The number of currently stored macro variations. Available since Live 11.0.
Get/set the currently selected variation. Available since Live 11.0.
The number of currently visible macros.

Parameters: source_index [int] destination_index [int] Copies all content of a Drum Rack pad from a source pad to a destination pad. The source_index and destination_index refer to pad indices inside a Drum Rack.
Increases the number of visible macro controls. Available since Live 11.0.

Parameters: index [int] (optional) Attempts to insert a new chain at the given index, or at the end of the chain list if no index is provided. Throws an error if insertion is not possible. Available since Live 12.3.
Decreases the number of visible macro controls. Available since Live 11.0.
Randomizes the values of eligible macro controls. Available since Live 11.0.
Stores a new variation of the values of all currently mapped macros. Available since Live 11.0.
Recalls the currently selected macro variation. Available since Live 11.0.
Recalls the macro variation that was recalled most recently. Available since Live 11.0.
Deletes the currently selected macro variation. Does nothing if there is no selected variation. Available since Live 11.0.

C74-LOM-RACKDEVICE_VIEW.text: Represents the view aspects of a Rack Device. A RackDevice.View is a type of Device.View, meaning that it has all the properties that a Device.View has. Listed below are the members unique to RackDevice.View.
Currently selected Drum Rack pad. Only available for Drum Racks.
Lowest row of pads visible, range: 0 - 28. Only available for Drum Racks.
1 = the devices in the currently selected chain are visible.

C74-LOM-CHAIN.text: This class represents a group device chain in Live.
live_set tracks N devices M chains L
live_set tracks N devices M return_chains L
live_set tracks N devices M chains L devices K chains P ...
live_set tracks N devices M return_chains L devices K chains P ...

The RGB value of the chain's color in the form 0x00rrggbb or (2^16 * red) + (2^8) * green + blue, where red, green and blue are values from 0 (dark) to 255 (light). When setting the RGB value, the nearest color from the color chooser is taken.
The color index of the chain.
1 = the chain will always have the color of the containing track or chain.
1 = muted due to another chain being soloed.
1 = soloed (Solo switch on) does not automatically turn Solo off in other chains.
Parameter: index [int] Delete the device at the given index.

Parameters: device_name [symbol] target_index [int] (optional) Attempts to insert the device specified by device_name at the given index in the chain. If no index is provided, attempts to insert the device at the end. Throws an error if insertion is not possible. device_name is the name as it appears in the UI of Live. Not all indices are valid. As can be expected, indices outside of the range defined by the current length of the device chain are invalid, but there are other limitations: for example, a MIDI effect can't be inserted after an instrument. The rule of thumb is that if an index would be invalid when inserting using the mouse, it's invalid here. At the moment, only native Live devices can be inserted. Max for Live devices and plug-in are not supported. Available since Live 12.3.

C74-LOM-DRUMCHAIN.text: This class represents a Drum Rack device chain in Live. A DrumChain is a type of Chain, meaning that it has all the children, properties and functions that a Chain has. Listed below are the members unique to DrumChain.
Get/set the MIDI note that will trigger this chain. The value -1 corresponds to the "All Notes" setting in the UI. Available since Live 12.3
Get/set the MIDI note sent to the devices in the chain.

1 = soloed (Solo switch on) Does not automatically turn Solo off in other chains.
